answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when a randomly sampled task fails independent verification. The verifier checks signed outputs against a hidden test set, so copying one honest answer across many accounts does not establish reliability. Splitting influence across sybils therefore multiplies the capital at risk without multiplying useful work; a dune survey or bridge repair might earn trust, while a zephyr of disposable accounts faces repeated deposits and losses.
